title: Cyber security and cyber security management system
scope_summary: Approves vehicle types with regard to cyber security, which requires a valid Certificate of Compliance for the manufacturer's Cyber Security Management System (CSMS). It applies to vehicles of Categories M and N, Category O if fitted with at least one electronic control unit, and Categories L6 and L7 if equipped with automated driving functionalities from level 3 onwards.
scope_quote: 1.1 This Regulation applies to vehicles, with regard to cyber security, of the Categories M and N. This Regulation also applies to vehicles of Category O if fitted with at least one electronic control unit. 1.2 This Regulation also applies to vehicles of the Categories L6 and L7 if equipped with automated driving functionalities from level 3 onwards, as defined in the reference document with definitions of Automated Driving under WP.29 and the General Principles for developing a UN Regulation on automated vehicles (ECE/TRANS/WP.29/1140).
vehicle_categories: O (if fitted with at least one electronic control unit)
L6 (if equipped with automated driving functionalities from level 3 onwards)
L7 (if equipped with automated driving functionalities from level 3 onwards)
applies_to_components: External interfaces of the vehicle with respect to cyber security
Electrical or electronic components and their functions (protection from cyber threats)
Systems (sets of components and/or sub-systems implementing functions)
Manufacturer's Cyber Security Management System (organisational processes, responsibilities, governance)
relation_to_other_regulations: Without prejudice to other UN Regulations, regional or national legislation governing access by authorized parties to the vehicle, its data, functions and resources (para 1.3)
Without prejudice to national and regional legislation on privacy and protection of personal data (para 1.3)

Without prejudice to other UN Regulations, national or regional legislation governing development and installation/system integration of replacement parts and components, physical and digital, with regard to cybersecurity (para 1.4)
Refers to ECE/TRANS/WP.29/1140 for the definition of automated driving levels (para 1.2)
Approval mark may be combined with marks of other Regulations under which the vehicle type is approved (para 4.2)

defined_terms.label: Vehicle type
defined_terms.definition: Vehicles which do not differ in the manufacturer's designation of the vehicle type and in essential aspects of the electric/electronic architecture and external interfaces with respect to cyber security.

defined_terms.label: Cyber security
defined_terms.definition: The condition in which road vehicles and their functions are protected from cyber threats to electrical or electronic components.

defined_terms.label: Cyber Security Management System (CSMS)
defined_terms.definition: A systematic risk-based approach defining organisational processes, responsibilities and governance to treat risk associated with cyber threats to vehicles and protect them from cyber-attacks.

defined_terms.label: System
defined_terms.definition: A set of components and/or sub-systems that implements a function or functions.

defined_terms.label: Development phase
defined_terms.definition: The period before a vehicle type is type approved.

defined_terms.label: Production phase
defined_terms.definition: The duration of production of a vehicle type.

defined_terms.label: Post-production phase
defined_terms.definition: The period from when a vehicle type is no longer produced until the end-of-life of all vehicles under the vehicle type.

defined_terms.label: Mitigation
defined_terms.definition: A measure that is reducing risk.

defined_terms.label: Risk
defined_terms.definition: The potential that a given threat will exploit vulnerabilities of a vehicle and thereby cause harm to the organization or to an individual.

defined_terms.label: Risk Assessment
defined_terms.definition: The overall process of risk identification, risk analysis and risk evaluation to determine whether a risk is acceptable or tolerable.

defined_terms.label: Risk Management
defined_terms.definition: Coordinated activities to direct and control an organization with regard to risk.

defined_terms.label: Threat
defined_terms.definition: A potential cause of an unwanted incident, which may result in harm to a system, organization or individual.

defined_terms.label: Vulnerability
defined_terms.definition: A weakness of an asset or mitigation that can be exploited by one or more threats.

applicability_hints: The regulation approves vehicle types, not components; a component falls under it indirectly when it is part of the vehicle's electric/electronic architecture or external interfaces relevant to cyber security.
A trailer (Category O) is pulled into scope by having even a single electronic control unit (e.g. EBS/ABS modulator, telematics unit).

Any ECU or electronic component with an external interface (e.g. diagnostic port, wireless/cellular, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, USB, charging communication, V2X) is likely relevant to the vehicle risk assessment and the Annex 5 threat catalogue.

Suppliers are affected via the manufacturer's CSMS and documentation duties: para 3.2.2 requires the manufacturer or its suppliers to make sufficient information available for the checks, even if covered by IP rights.
Back-end servers and off-board systems communicating with the vehicle are addressed via Annex 5 (mitigations outside the vehicle), so connected services can be relevant.
Changes to the E/E architecture or external interfaces may create a new vehicle type or require extension under para 8.
Aftermarket/replacement parts are not directly regulated: para 1.4 leaves them to other legislation.
L6/L7 quadricycles are only in scope if they have level 3+ automated driving functions.
